responses: I'm VoxAssist, a responsive speech bot built as a Deep Learning course project.
You can call me VoxAssist. I combine a neural-network intent classifier with speech input and spoken replies.

responses: I can answer questions about this project and common study topics. You can type a message or use the microphone, and I can read my reply aloud.
Try asking about deep learning, speech recognition, text to speech, neural networks, model training, study tips, or this project. Use the quick prompts below for examples.

patterns: what does this speech bot do

what is the purpose of voxassist
explain the whole system in simple words

what happens after I speak to the bot
responses: VoxAssist is a responsive speech bot. The browser converts speech to text, a Python backend classifies the message with a feed-forward neural network, and the browser can speak the answer aloud using text to speech.

The project demonstrates a complete speech interaction loop: microphone input, text transcription, neural-network intent classification, response selection, and optional spoken output. A text box remains available as a fallback.

responses: Deep learning is a machine-learning approach that uses neural networks with multiple layers to learn useful representations from data. In VoxAssist, a multilayer neural network learns to map text features to intent categories.
Think of deep learning as learning patterns through stacked computational layers. The model here receives a multi-hot vector of words and phrases, then predicts which intent best matches the message.

responses: A neural network consists of connected computational units with learnable weights. During training, it makes predictions, measures the error with a loss function, and updates weights through backpropagation and an optimizer.
VoxAssist uses a feed-forward network with two hidden layers and ReLU activations. Its final layer produces scores for the supported intent classes.

responses: Intent classification maps a message to a category such as greeting, deep learning, or study tips. VoxAssist converts the text into features, obtains class probabilities from its neural network, and selects a response for the predicted intent.
The model predicts one of the intent labels defined in intents.json. If its confidence is below a threshold, the bot uses a fallback response instead of pretending it understood.

responses: Speech recognition converts spoken audio into text. In this project, the browser's Web Speech API handles transcription, and the resulting text is sent to the Flask backend for intent classification.

The microphone button starts browser speech recognition. When a final transcript is available, VoxAssist sends the words to its local Python server. Recognition support depends on the browser and its speech service.

responses: Text to speech converts written text into spoken audio. VoxAssist uses the browser's SpeechSynthesis API to read bot replies aloud, so a separate speech-generation model is not required.
Use the Voice Replies control to enable or disable spoken answers. The browser and operating system provide the available voices.

patterns: what happens when I run train py

responses: Run python train.py to train the classifier. It builds a vocabulary from the patterns in intents.json, vectorizes examples, trains a multilayer perceptron with cross-entropy loss and Adam, and saves the model weights and metadata under artifacts/.

The training script uses supervised learning: each example text is paired with an intent label. The model produces logits, cross-entropy measures classification error, and Adam updates the parameters by backpropagation.

responses: The dataset is intents.json. Each intent contains a tag, example patterns, and possible responses. Add several varied patterns to teach a category, then rerun python train.py to rebuild the model.
This is a small, hand-curated educational dataset rather than a large public benchmark. It is editable, making it easy to demonstrate how more examples can improve intent coverage.

Break a difficult topic into concepts, work through one example, explain it in your own words, and test yourself later. Keep your phone away during focus sessions.

responses: A strong report can cover the problem statement, objectives, related work, system architecture, dataset and preprocessing, neural-network design, training procedure, evaluation metrics, interface, limitations, and future work. patterns: how do I fix my mic

responses: Check that you are using a supported browser such as recent Chrome or Edge, open the app at http://127.0.0.1:5000, and allow microphone permission. Also check Windows microphone privacy settings and your selected input device.

The app can still be tested with typed messages. For speech input, try Chrome or Edge, allow microphone access, confirm Windows recognizes your microphone, and reload the page. Speech recognition availability can depend on your browser and internet connection.

responses: Recent Chrome or Edge on desktop is recommended for the Web Speech API. The page layout adapts to smaller screens, but speech-recognition support varies by browser and operating system; typed input is the fallback.

The Flask app and neural-network prediction run locally. Browser speech recognition may use an online service, so the full voice workflow is not guaranteed to work offline. The interface itself is responsive on mobile-sized screens.

responses: The Flask backend processes the text you submit and does not save chat history or microphone recordings. Browser speech recognition may send audio to a browser-vendor service depending on its implementation, so avoid sensitive information and check your browser's privacy settings.

Intent classification runs on your local Python server. The browser handles microphone transcription and spoken output; Web Speech recognition may rely on an online service. This demo does not include a database or persistent chat storage.
